cohort: The study included 220,169 twin deliveries and 270,540 singleton deliveries from the U.S. Natality Database (2007-2010) with gestational ages of 37 to 42 weeks, excluding those with congenital anomalies.
finding: Twins have a higher risk of suboptimal neonatal outcomes compared to singletons and do best when delivered at early term (37-38 weeks) rather than term or late term.
